subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Does the supported Admin HTTP RPC threat model permit configuration-changing browser requests under trusted-proxy or explicit no-auth deployments without an Origin or anti-CSRF check?
rationale: Source establishes a sensitive HTTP mutation surface but not whether every supported authentication and browser networking mode supplies a non-ambient credential or otherwise blocks a forged cross-origin POST.

options.title: Validate and harden the HTTP owner
options.body: Reproduce the route under each supported auth mode and add narrowly scoped request-origin or CSRF enforcement where browser ambient authentication can reach mutations.

options.title: Confirm the existing boundary
options.body: Close only after security owners demonstrate that supported browser requests cannot authenticate cross-origin and document that invariant with focused tests.

recommendation.title: Validate and harden the HTTP owner
recommendation.body: Reproduce the route under each supported auth mode and add narrowly scoped request-origin or CSRF enforcement where browser ambient authentication can reach mutations.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history connects this contributor to the original ACP bridge plus subsequent Gateway authentication and secret-handling hardening.
